display_name: d'Arenberg The High Trellis Cabernet Sauvignon, McLaren Vale
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "High trellis training exposes McLaren Vale Cabernet clusters to direct sunlight, speeding ripening and concentrating blackcurrant flavors in this d'Arenberg bottling. That setup counters the region's warm afternoons with better airflow, yielding softer tannins than Bordeaux counterparts. At 14.5% ABV in the 2020, it punches above its everyday price.",
  "wine_summary": "d'Arenberg crafts this Cabernet from estate vines planted to high trellis systems, a nod to managing McLaren Vale's heat for even ripeness. The producer skips fining and filtration across its range, letting terroir drive the show—Chester Osborn's hands-off approach amplifies site differences. This wine stands out in a sea of ripe Australian reds because its structure holds up over years, thanks to old-vine depth and coastal moderation.",
  "terroir_expression": "Terra rossa soils over limestone in McLaren Vale deliver iron-rich minerality and firm acidity to the wine's black plum core, while dark cracking clays retain moisture for sustained ripeness without flab. Maritime winds from Gulf St Vincent cool nights after 35°C days, preserving green pepper pyrazines alongside cassis. Elevations from 50 to 350 meters add gradient-driven freshness, translating to graphite-edged fruit in the glass.",
  "vinification_summary": "Foot-trodden and basket-pressed, the must ferments with indigenous yeasts in open fermenters, extracting grippy tannins without harshness. Extended maceration—skins stay on for 4-6 weeks—builds color and structure; malolactic follows naturally. Basket pressing (using old-school wooden presses) minimizes oxygen pickup, preserving primary fruit while integrating oak from used barrels.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled kangaroo skewers with bush tomato relish— the wine's dark chocolate notes match the char, tannins cut gaminess. Nashville hot chicken—riper blackcurrant tempers spice, acidity slices fried coating. Braised beef cheek with parsnip puree—plush body melds with slow-cooked richness, graphite cuts fat. Charcuterie of prosciutto and aged cheddar—cedar echoes cured meat, firm structure stands up to salt.",
  "comparable_wines": "Yalumba D'Arry's Original Shiraz Grenache — shares McLaren Vale warmth and value-driven ripeness with softer edges. Kilikanoon Oracle Shiraz — similar old-vine concentration and coastal balance at comparable depth.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry Cabernet with ripe tannins and mineral drive",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2020 from now through 2030; store horizontally in 55-60°F darkness. Earlier vintages like 2013 hit peak now.",
  "value_assessment": "$25-35 retail positions it against Penfolds Bin 2 Cabernet, which costs more for less site focus. Worth buying over Napa entry-levels at this price—superior structure justifies cellaring. Skip if chasing sub-$20 bargains.",
  "market_position": "American steakhouse lists favor it for pairing punch without premium markup. Retail shelves target casual Cabernet fans upgrading from $15 bottles. Aussie wine bars pour it to newcomers wary of Shiraz dominance.",
  "insider_take": "Most overlook how high trellis tames McLaren Vale's heat for Bordeaux-like tension— this beats Coonawarra Cabs on fruit purity. Skip if you hate green pepper notes; otherwise, stock up for winter roasts. Tradeoff is shorter-term drinkability versus Napa's oak bombast.",
  "aging_potential_years": 12,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,

    "color_intensity": "deep",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",

  }
}
